title: USMCA Trade Rupture Tracker Update — Sep 14, 2026
summary: In the most optimistic signal from either government since the Aug 21 talks collapse, Trump said Sept 12 in Dublin that a US-Canada deal could come 'fairly soon' once Canada addresses dairy market-access issues, repeating a disputed 400%-tariff claim that Canadian trade advisor Ralph Goodale called factually wrong. PM Carney responded Sept 14, telling Bloomberg 'I welcome the president's comments' and that he remains open to a deal respecting Canadian sovereignty, with 'not a pride thing' in the way. Carney made the remarks while opening his Canada Investment Summit in Toronto, drawing roughly 300 CEOs managing over $120 trillion in assets to pitch Canada as an alternative to US-bound investment, ahead of a planned address to the European Parliament. Canada's TSX rebounded 191.21 points (+0.54%) on Sept 11 after a three-session slide. No new formal bilateral talks have been confirmed as resumed, and the Sept 8 tariffs and import bans on both sides remain in effect. Timeline, KPIs, map lines, map points, econ, claims and political sections updated.

title: USMCA Trade Rupture Tracker Update — Sep 11, 2026
summary: PM Carney signaled Sept 10 that Canada would hold off further retaliation for now, calling Washington's Sept 8 bans on Canadian dairy, alcohol and motor vehicle imports 'relatively modest' compared with earlier US actions, while saying he remains in regular contact with Trump on unrelated files like Ukraine and Iran. That restraint came alongside a fresh flashpoint: Trump threatened Sept 7 to ban Bombardier aircraft sales in the US unless the company builds domestically, which Bombardier disputed by citing its 3,500 US employees across 47 states. Finance Minister Champagne said Canada-US officials remain in contact as the TSX fell to an eight-day low Sept 9, and former ambassador Kirsten Hillman said formal talks may not resume for months given Canada's red lines on steel and autos. In Mexico City, Sheinbaum and Lutnick held a virtual USMCA call Sept 9 after weather grounded Lutnick's flight, both sides calling it 'cordial' ahead of the fourth bilateral review round. Timeline, KPIs, map lines, map points, econ, claims and political sections updated.

title: USMCA Trade Rupture Tracker Update — Sep 4, 2026
summary: With Canada's C$27.6 billion retaliatory tariffs still on track for Sept 8, the US and Canada spent early September trading public blame instead of negotiating. Commerce Secretary Lutnick said Sept 3 that Canada invented 'crazy ideas' to walk away from talks for domestic political reasons tied to Quebec's provincial election and Alberta's referendum; PM Carney, speaking from Thunder Bay, rejected the claim and said US negotiators had themselves shifted red-line positions since the Aug 21 collapse. Trump followed with a Truth Social warning that Carney would regret making him 'the enemy.' Carney separately said Sept 1 that US demands aimed to 'wipe out' Canadian industries or turn them into subsidiaries. In Mexico City, President Sheinbaum said Sept 3 her government was 'working very hard' on a better steel, aluminum and auto deal ahead of the fourth bilateral round, while maintaining Mexico's non-retaliation posture. No new US-Canada talks are scheduled. Timeline, KPIs, map lines, map points, econ, claims and political sections updated.

title: USMCA Trade Rupture Tracker Update — Aug 25, 2026
summary: Trump escalated Aug 24, posting on Truth Social that Canada must 'fall in line' or face consequences 'far WORSE,' threatening new 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles, trucks, auto parts and steel starting Jan 1, 2027, and referring to Carney as 'Governor Carney.' Carney rejected the framing, saying Canada would not accept being treated as 'a subsidiary of the United States' and that the US wanted to 'destroy our major industries.' Ottawa responded Aug 25 by finalizing its retaliation package: Finance Minister Champagne, Industry Minister Joly, Jobs Minister Hajdu and AI Minister Solomon detailed a sliding 15/25/50% tariff scale on C$27.6 billion of US goods, paired with a C$7.5 billion worker and business support package including expanded EI eligibility — both effective September 8. Timeline, KPIs, map lines, map points, claims and political sections updated.

title: USMCA Trade Rupture Tracker Update — Aug 23, 2026
summary: US-Canada trade talks collapsed late Aug 21, hours before the deadline, after Carney called last-minute US terms 'uneconomic, unfair' and Greer accused Canada of walking back agreed commitments. The paused 50% Section 338 tariffs took legal effect at 12:01am ET Aug 22, hitting roughly $20 billion (C$28 billion) of Canadian goods across electronics, dairy, alcohol, cement and other sectors. Carney suspended negotiations, recalled Canada's negotiators, declared 'You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked,' and announced dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp/paper and electronics effective September 8. KPIs, timeline, map lines, map points, claims and political sections updated to reflect the collapse and new escalation.
